content: Tylenol PM is a brand name for a combination of two active ingredients: paracetamol (also known as acetaminophen) and diphenhydramine. This product is manufactured and distributed by Johnson & Johnson. It is marketed as a dual-purpose medication, functioning as both an analgesic (pain reliever) and a sedative (sleep aid). Tylenol PM is specifically designed to alleviate occasional headaches and minor aches or pains that are accompanied by sleeplessness. It is labeled as non-habit-forming. Acetaminophen, when sold on its own, is marketed under the name Tylenol. Diphenhydramine, when sold independently, is marketed under names such as Simply Sleep and Benadryl. Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine and serves as the active ingredient in Benadryl, which is used to treat allergies, as well as in Benylin, a medication used for cough and cold therapy. In the latter, it acts as an antitussive (anti-cough agent) and provides a drying effect due to its antihistamine properties. The sedative effect of diphenhydramine, which causes drowsiness, is a result of its antihistamine action. Tylenol PM has also been implicated in the production of a drug known as Cheese, which is a combination of Tylenol PM and black tar heroin. This drug has gained popularity among young teenagers in the Dallas, Texas area. In response to this issue, some stores in the Dallas region have removed Tylenol PM from their shelves. This decision was made because store managers suspected that individuals involved in the production of Cheese were shoplifting Tylenol PM to use as an ingredient in the drug.
